subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in session PIN tool gate, and what trusted secret source, verifier path, and reset semantics define that security boundary?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose the product/security contract for a new auth gate that affects tool execution, secret handling, session state, and prompt-injection hardening.

options.title: Sponsor a core security design
options.body: Define a core opt-in PIN/secret-source contract, trusted TypeScript verifier, session-authenticated state, reset semantics, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep it plugin-only for now
options.body: Document how a plugin can use before_tool_call, accepting that deployments must own the verifier and session-state semantics themselves.

options.title: Reject this boundary
options.body: Close the request if maintainers decide OpenClaw's personal-assistant trust model should not add a per-session PIN gate.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core security design
recommendation.body: Define a core opt-in PIN/secret-source contract, trusted TypeScript verifier, session-authenticated state, reset semantics, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a security/auth boundary choice, and the available history plus security-sensitive ownership points closest to steipete for routing.
